newsitem.title: UK: Two more UK loan providers get stock listing nod.
newsitem.headline: Two more UK loan providers get stock listing nod.

text.p: British home loan and savings organisations, the Northern Rock and Bristol & West Building Society, voted on Tuesday to shed their mutually owned status in the latest moves in reshaping of the country's financial services industry.
Borrowers and savers in the two societies will be amongst the 15 million people receiving free shares from the British building societies converting to banks this year.
In February, Britain's largest home loan provider, Halifax Building Society, got its members' approval to float on the market at a value of some 12 billion pounds.
Two other institutions, Woolwich and Alliance & Leicester, will also convert to bank status in coming months.
About 97 percent of 900,000 members of Northern Rock voted in favour of the conversion which would give them an average 500 shares when the society floats on the stock exchange later this year.
Members of Bristol & West voted in favour of its merger with the Bank of Ireland which was agreed last year for the bank to take over the building society for 600 million pounds ($972.6 million).
About one million members of Britain's ninth largest building society will receive either cash or shares with long-term members receiving an average of 1,100 pounds in cash.
On March 20, the British parliament passed a new Buildings Societies Act which would allow societies to compete on level footing with all other financial institutions.

But the new law was criticised by some of the building societies planning to convert since it removes a converting society's five-year immunity from takeover if the new bank buys another financial institution or if 75 percent of the shareholders vote to abandon it.

Apart from the share offer, Northern Rock will also pay a statutory cash bonus of around 8.8 percent of balances held in accounts on December 31, 1996 to those members who are not entitled to vote including those under 18 years of age.
Northern Rock, with a history that dates back to 1850s, is expected to be floated on October 1.

"We are extremely pleased that so many of our investing and borrowing members took part in the voting process and that the board's conversion proposals received such an overwhelming endorsement", its chairman Robert Dickenson said.
"We will continue to compete aggressively for (their) loyalty and we look forward to maintain the relationship with them both as customers and Northern Rock Plc shareholders," he said.
The estimated market price of the shares has been pegged between 260 and 295 pence. ($ = 0.616 British Pounds)
